# Critique — Pattern 12 (Recovery & Sleep)

The slot allocation across the 255 slots was distributed as follows: Sleep Duration & Timing (~15%), Sleep Quality & Disorders (~15%), Sleep Aids & Environment (~15%), Routines, Alertness, & Stress (~20%), Recovery Modalities, Overtraining, & Dreams (~25%), and self-monitoring fillers (~10%). Filling the 255 slots was relatively straightforward due to the wide range of physiological sleep parameters and recovery tools; a few tracking questions at the end (positions 245–255) served as minor fillers. Overlaps exist with the Respiratory and Mental Health domains (e.g., sleep apnea, clinical insomnia, CPAP usage) because sleep apnea is primarily a respiratory disorder with huge sleep impact, and insomnia is tightly bound to psychiatric state. The V-flag was systematically set to `true` on questions where a "Yes" answer indicates healthy, protective sleep habits or recovery practices (e.g., 7-9 hours sleep, bedtime routines, tracking sleep HRV, rest days) to maintain a polarity where `1` represents sleep disruption or risk. We paraphrased elements of the Epworth Sleepiness Scale and STOP-BANG to avoid verbatim reproduction of copyrighted scales. The weakest question is position 253 ("Do you log your recovery & sleep symptoms weekly...") as it is a generic template fallback that adds little clinical signal.
